prompt: A carpenter wants to prove that two rafters are parallel. She measures angles where a single straight strut crosses both rafters. Which measurement would PROVE the rafters are parallel?

choices.label: A pair of alternate interior angles each measure $63^\circ$
A pair of co-interior (same-side interior) angles each measure $63^\circ$
A pair of alternate interior angles measure $63^\circ$ and $117^\circ$
The two rafters are cut to the same length

hint: Each parallel-line theorem has a converse that works backwards: measure the angles, conclude the lines are parallel.

hints.text: Each parallel-line theorem has a converse that works backwards: measure the angles, conclude the lines are parallel.
Alternate interior angles must be CONGRUENT for parallel lines; co-interior angles must be SUPPLEMENTARY.
Two congruent alternate interior angles ($63^\circ$ each) prove the rafters are parallel.

explanation: The Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem says: if alternate interior angles are congruent, the lines are parallel.
Choice A gives exactly that — two congruent alternate interior angles.

Choice B fails because co-interior angles would need to add to $180^\circ$, and $63 + 63 = 126$. Choice C has alternate interior angles that are not equal, and choice D says nothing about direction — two boards of equal length can point any which way.

alternativeExplanations.title: Flip the theorem around
steps: Forward: parallel lines ⇒ congruent alternate interior angles.
Backward (the converse): congruent alternate interior angles ⇒ parallel lines. Carpenters use the backward version, because they can measure angles but cannot measure "forever."
